pull.title: test: Set socket timeout in interface_http.py
pull.body:
This should help to debug/fix https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/issues/368, but seems independently useful to avoid unbounded-time test runs.


Also rework the `413`-code tests where a pre-existing issue was made more likely by the first commit.

test: Set socket timeout in interface_http.py

Currently, the socket timeout in BitcoinHTTPConnection is not set, and
sometimes reset (redundantly) to None.

Fix both issues by using the RPC timeout of the node, which should be
large enough to cover all use-cases.

Specific tests can still call set_timeout() if they need to.

test: Rework 413 Too Large tests in interface_http.py

The tests had a few small problems:

* The comment claimed that the send operation was blocking until
  timeout. However, a send should terminate once the server closes the
  socket.
* The test possibly force-closed the connection, instead of testing the
  outcome that the server closes it.
* The test tried to read a "413 Content too large", but such an outcome
  is not guaranteed when the server is closing the connection.

Fix all issues, by adjusting the comments and asserting the server
closes the connection.  The error code is only asserted in the debug
log.

events.body: Hmm, I guess with a timeout the socket can go through `select()` and then manifest this race. Still, the test seems like it should be fixed and only assert the essential outcome: 413 logged and socket closed. I'll push a commit for that ...

Heh, looks like this accidentally fixes https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/issues/368.

At least according to @pinheadmz's Fable, IIUC: https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/issues/368#issuecomment-6059544560

ACK fa5551cc6de1629ef800d8b1f7697af923a953bb

Built and tested on macos/arm64 as well as NetBSD VM in qemu, I know its not OpenBSD but its what i had lying around. Also ran the intermittent test on a loop in an OpenBSD ci: https://github.com/pinheadmz/bitcoin/actions/runs/37847855161

Reviewed the changes, came to the same conclusion that the connection needed a timeout set before the first `connect()`. I'm a little nervous that without a catch / retry we'll end up with a flaky test again but then we might have more data to diagnose with.

Change to the excessive size test makes sense as well - using the server log to assert something happened is more reliable than waiting for an event on the client side to tell us what happened.
